name: Diaphragmatic or Abdominal Wall Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Diaphragmatic or Abdominal Wall Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of a congenital defect in the diaphragm or abdominal wall confirmed by imaging or surgery
Herniation of abdominal organs into the thoracic cavity or through the abdominal wall defect
Respiratory distress or compromised pulmonary function in the neonatal period
Prenatal ultrasound evidence of diaphragmatic or abdominal wall defect

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a congenital diaphragmatic or abdominal wall defect with herniation of abdominal contents confirmed by imaging or surgical exploration
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made prenatally or immediately postnatally due to respiratory compromise.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital diaphragmatic defect with herniation of abdominal viscera
pathognomonic.notes: Typically identified by imaging or surgery
searchTerms: diaphragm defect with abdominal organs in chest

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible abdominal wall defect with externalized abdominal contents
pathognomonic.notes: Commonly seen in gastroschisis or omphalocele
searchTerms: abdominal wall defect with exposed contents

common.symptomName: Neonatal respiratory distress due to pulmonary hypoplasia
searchTerms: newborn breathing difficulty from small lungs
respiratory distress due to lung underdevelopment
pulmonary hypoplasia causing neonatal breathing problems

common.symptomName: Scaphoid (sunken) abdomen due to abdominal contents displacement

searchTerms: poor sucking or swallowing in neonates

occasional.notes: Due to feeding and respiratory issues
searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

laboratory: Arterial blood gas abnormalities indicating hypoxia and acidosis
Elevated lactate in severe respiratory compromise
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing diaphragmatic or abdominal wall defect
Chest X-ray demonstrating herniation of abdominal contents into thoracic cavity
MRI or CT confirming defect size and organ displacement
genetic: No consistent single gene mutation; may be associated with chromosomal abnormalities or syndromes
other: Surgical findings confirming defect type and extent
Pulmonary function testing showing restrictive lung disease

distinguishingFeatures: Lung cystic lesions without herniation of abdominal organs
Abdominal wall defect covered by a membranous sac

redFlags: Severe neonatal respiratory distress refractory to oxygen therapy
Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
Failure to thrive despite nutritional support
references: Pober BR. Overview of epidemiology, genetics, birth defects, and pathophysiology of congenital diaphragmatic hernia. UpToDate. 2023.
